specFileAssertionAuthorshipFinding.status: WRITTEN 2026-09-21, at the team lead's request, after the sixth instance of the same authorship defect surfaced in e2e/mega-menu-f8-logo-and-tickets-rail.spec.ts within one feature's QA pass. This is a finding about how THIS FILE'S assertions were written, not a seventh incident note -- the six incidents are cited by id below and their individual fixes are recorded at contract-f8.yaml A3/A7/A8/A4/A20/A12 and this golden's/f8-lead-logo.json's own defect rulings; this entry exists to state what they have in common and what that implies.
instances: A12 -- the 400px/200px source-resolution floor is two independent literal arguments with no code-level expression tying one to the other (literalCouplingRisk, f8-lead-logo.json)

A1-A3 -- domLoadVerificationRequirement was written as a binding requirement on A1-A3 before F8a existed, then F8a landed and A1-A3 shipped without it; caught by re-inspection, not a gate (closed as A20)
A3 -- 'venue/date meta line still renders below the logo' built a leadTrack locator, never used it, and asserted an unrelated element's position instead
A7 -- 'meta line is NOS olive-700' used a `rail.locator('span')` selector broad enough to miss its own target and narrow enough that its `if (count>0)` guard silently never ran
A8 -- 'no NOS colour appears anywhere outside the tickets rail' checked three hand-picked elements against one of four registered NOS colours
A4 -- 'renders exactly three destination links' asserted three named links' hrefs and never measured the rail's total link count, so a fourth link would pass
specFileAssertionAuthorshipFinding.diagnosis: In every one of the six, the test's TITLE states a specific, checkable property (the meta line renders; the colour resolves to olive-700; no NOS colour appears ANYWHERE; EXACTLY three links), and the test's BODY was written to make Playwright report green, without anyone checking that the body's assertions actually entail the title's claim. The titles were written as claims about the feature; the bodies were written to pass. Nothing in how this file was authored or reviewed checked that the second thing proved the first -- three instances were an assertion pointed at the wrong element entirely (A3, A4's missing count), one was a selector broad enough to defeat its own guard (A7), one was a coverage gap dressed as a universal claim (A8), and one was a cross-file requirement that nothing enforced at the moment it came due (A1-A3/A20). Different mechanisms, same root cause: title-writing and body-writing were not checked against each other.
specFileAssertionAuthorshipFinding.systematicDetectionOptions: What would catch this class going forward, stated honestly about each option's limits rather than proposed as a solved problem. A static title-vs-body lint (matching the English claim in a test's name against the properties its assertions actually check) is not reliably automatable -- these are natural-language claims, and building a linter that understands 'exactly three' implies a `.toHaveCount(3)` call, or that 'anywhere' implies exhaustive element coverage, is a much harder problem than the defects it would catch, and a lint loose enough to be buildable would miss most of these six. A narrower structural rule -- 'no conditional guard may skip silently, only via a visible test.skip()' -- is real and worth keeping (it is now A21's standing requirement), but it only catches instance A7 (case 4); it says nothing about A3 (wrong element, no guard at all), A8 (undercoverage, no guard), A4 (missing assertion, no guard), or A1-A3/A20 (a requirement nothing enforced, not a guard). An unused-variable lint sounds promising for A3 specifically, but was already defeated in the actual code by a deliberate `void leadTrack;` -- the exact silencing idiom a lint exists to catch is also the idiom that evades it when a human writes it on purpose to quiet a warning rather than to fix the mismatch it's warning about. Mutation testing (does the test still pass if the property it claims is deliberately broken -- delete the meta line, add a fourth link, forge the colour) is the one approach that would generalize across all six, because it directly tests title-claim-sensitivity rather than guessing at intent from names or code shape; but it requires someone to already write the mutants (delete this element, add this extra link), which requires the same judgment call a reviewer makes reading the title and asking 'does the body prove this' -- it moves the problem, it does not remove it, and this project's toolchain has no mutation-testing infrastructure today, so proposing it here would be inventing a process nobody is positioned to run.
specFileAssertionAuthorshipFinding.conclusion: The only thing that actually caught these six, across every mechanism, was a reader -- human or model -- reading each test's title and asking whether its body proves it: three found by Codex's cross-model pass (A7, A8, A4), three by direct human re-inspection (A12, A1-A3/A20, A3). Zero were caught by any contract gate, any lint, or any check that runs without a reader applying judgment. That is not an argument for adding more rules to this file -- the rules that exist (test.skip over silent guards, real getComputedStyle over source grep, stable data-testid locators over content-dependent ones) are all real and worth keeping, but none of them, individually or together, would have caught more than one or two of these six. It is a direct, concrete argument that the mandatory Codex GPT-5.5 pass (docs/rules/workflow.md) is load-bearing infrastructure for this specific defect class, not a ceremonial second opinion -- half of this feature's defects existed only because a second independent reader looked, and the other half existed only because a human did the same thing the mandatory pass exists to do systematically. Skipping that pass on a future feature would not just reduce review coverage in the abstract; on this file's own evidence, it would have let three of six real, title-contradicting defects ship.

scopeBoundary.rule: This is a deliberate, Brad-approved exception to the site's standing brand-architecture rule (project memory project_national_show_brand_architecture: 'SAOC chrome site-wide, Show branding below the header on /national-show'). It applies ONLY to the Tickets rail's own fill/text/button colours (Track 5 of the mega menu grid). Every other part of Header.tsx / MegaMenu.tsx / MobileMenu.tsx / nav-config.ts -- including the rail's own structural border-left, which is shared grid-track chrome, not rail content -- stays on the SAOC palette (app/globals.css's existing --color-* tokens). A future feature must NOT read this exception as license to bring NOS colours into the lead block, the three group columns, the trigger button, or the mobile drawer.
scopeBoundary.structuralBorderRuling: The rail's border-left (separating it from the Exhibit & Trade column) is part of F7's five-track grid-divider system (trackBorders in f7-layout4-visual-fidelity.json: 1px solid --rule-soft on every non-lead track). It stays --rule-soft (SAOC). Only the rail's OWN background, heading colour, meta-line colour, and the three destination rows' fill/border/text colours switch to NOS tokens.
scopeBoundary.typographyRuling: Colours only, per the team lead's dispatch heading ('bring in the NOS brand system... Colours:'). Do NOT import the artifact's own display face (Fraunces) or body face (Karla) -- that is a font-family change, which is out of scope here and would need its own next/font loader plus the same @theme wiring care F7's A7 already had to fix once. Keep the rail's existing font-family classes (font-serif for the heading, font-mono for the meta line, font-sans for the destination labels) exactly as F7 left them; only recolour.

tokensToRegister.verificationMethod: The e2e golden below reads REAL computed style (getComputedStyle background-color / color) on the rendered rail, not a source grep for the @theme declaration -- F7's A7 finding was specifically that a token can be declared and still resolve to nothing usable at runtime, so declaration presence alone proves nothing. Do not consider this requirement satisfied by grepping app/globals.css.

styleValueProvenanceNote: contracts/checks/menu-system-layout4-shared/check-style-values-sourced.mjs and check-no-nos-palette-mixing.mjs both operate on SOURCE FILES passed as argv (see their own header comments) -- they were run during this contract's authoring against components/chrome/MegaMenu.tsx and nav-config.ts as they exist TODAY (pre-F8) and both pass (no literals to find yet, since F8 is unimplemented). Neither checker needs a code change for F8: check-style-values-sourced.mjs's hex-literal scan and check-no-nos-palette-mixing.mjs's hex-literal scan both only ever look for LITERAL #rrggbb strings in the files given to them. Because this golden requires the four hex values above to live ONLY in app/globals.css's @theme block (never as inline hex or arbitrary-value Tailwind syntax like bg-[#211a57] inside MegaMenu.tsx or nav-config.ts), MegaMenu.tsx and nav-config.ts carry ZERO NOS hex literals after F8 lands -- both checkers, run against those two files post-F8, must still exit 0. This is the assertion that actually proves the scope boundary held (see contract A5/A6) -- app/globals.css itself is deliberately NEVER passed to check-no-nos-palette-mixing.mjs (a plain hex-scan of an already-mixed-by-design stylesheet would trivially fail and prove nothing; the checker's job is to guard the CHROME COMPONENTS, which is exactly what A5/A6 exercise).

duplicateLinkRuling.issue: Found by @dev during F8b implementation (2026-09-11): the lead block's pre-existing 'The Show' group (unchanged by F8 -- see f8-lead-logo.json's reading.theShowGroupRuling) already renders its own 'Tickets' leaf, href /national-show/tickets, description 'Buy admission tickets.' (nav-config.ts, F1). The rail's new primary destination row ALSO renders label 'Tickets', href /national-show/tickets. Two distinct <a> elements, identical accessible name, identical href, both visible in the same open panel.
duplicateLinkRuling.ruling: This is INTENTIONAL, not a defect -- a quick-nav leaf inside 'The Show' group (alongside Show Sponsors, Past Shows, etc.) and a prominent CTA row in the feature rail are two different affordances in two different visual regions serving the same destination; duplicate links to the same href with the same name are common and not a WCAG violation (WCAG 2.4.4 concerns a link's name being ambiguous about its OWN destination, not two different links sharing a destination). Do not rename the rail's 'Tickets' label and do not remove or rename theShow's 'Tickets' leaf to avoid the collision -- both goldens (f8-lead-logo.json's theShowGroupRuling and this file's destinations.items) stand as originally written.
duplicateLinkRuling.testFix: e2e/mega-menu-f8-logo-and-tickets-rail.spec.ts was the thing that needed to change, not the data/markup: every rail-scoped link lookup is now scoped through a getRail(panel) helper (locates the rail's own container via its 'Tickets' <h4> ancestor) instead of querying panel.getByRole('link', {name: 'Tickets'}) unscoped, which hit a Playwright strict-mode violation (2 matches) before this fix. Applied directly by @architect to the golden spec file, not by @dev, per this mission's 'no@dev-edits-QA-inputs-or-goldens' rule.

metaLineTestDefectRuling.status: RULED 2026-09-21, contract-f8.yaml A7 amended (split) and A21 added. CORRECTED same day -- see `datasetStateCorrection` below: the dataset-null premise this ruling was originally written against was wrong.
metaLineTestDefectRuling.source: Codex GPT-5.5 cross-model review (mandatory per .claude/rules/workflow.md), finding 2 on e2e/mega-menu-f8-logo-and-tickets-rail.spec.ts's combined 'rail background is NOS pale-gold, meta line is NOS olive-700, structural border-left stays SAOC rule-soft' test -- worse than Codex's own framing, confirmed by direct read.
metaLineTestDefectRuling.finding: Verified directly (Read tool, spec file lines 290-314, plus MegaMenu.tsx:244-251/264): line 308 selects `rail.locator('span')` -- ANY span inside the rail, not the meta line specifically -- guarded by `if (metaCount > 0)` at line 310. The rail's three destination links render their label text directly inside <a> with no wrapping <span> (MegaMenu.tsx:264), so the meta line's own <span> (MegaMenu.tsx:245, rendered only `{featureRailMeta && (...)}`) is the ONLY span the rail can ever contain. This structural point is unaffected by the correction below -- it is a fact about the markup, not the data -- and it is why the guard's WIDTH (any span vs. the meta line specifically) was a real defect regardless of what featureRailMeta's value happened to be: even with the dates populated, `rail.locator('span')` would still be the wrong locator to standardize on going forward, because it would break silently again the moment a second span is ever added to the rail for any other reason.
metaLineTestDefectRuling.datasetStateCorrection: The original text of this ruling additionally claimed 'both showDate and showEndDate are null in the current dataset' and 'metaCount is 0 today, the guarded block never runs' -- both WRONG, retracted here. That claim was reached by reading MegaMenu.tsx:84-93's source comment and computation (a comment dated 2026-09-10, and code that reads a runtime value, neither of which can establish what that value currently IS) rather than by observing the live DOM. @dev's live instrumented run (2026-09-21) measured the real state directly: `metaCount: 1, text: "16–19 September 2027"` -- the dates ARE populated, and A21's colour assertion runs for real today; it does not skip. This is the same category of error the team lead separately flagged on A3's venueName claim (sourced from project memory rather than an observation) -- that one happened to be correct, this one was not, and both were avoidable with one page load. Per docs/rules/no-invention.md: never assert a runtime dataset state is true until a tool has shown it.
metaLineTestDefectRuling.fix: Split into two tests. A7 (amended) keeps only the background + border-left assertions, which are real and unconditional today -- test retitled to drop the meta-line claim it wasn't actually proving. A21 (new) is the meta-line colour check, given its own stable locator (data-testid="feature-rail-meta" on MegaMenu.tsx:245's span, replacing the bare `rail.locator('span')`), and required to use Playwright's runtime `test.skip(condition, reason)` API rather than an in-body `if` guard -- a skip must render as a visibly distinct SKIPPED result with a printed reason, not something that looks identical to a pass in the report. See contract-f8.yaml A21 for the full requirement.
metaLineTestDefectRuling.conditionalIsLegitimateHere: The `test.skip(condition, reason)` guard on A21 is retained regardless of today's data being populated -- its justification was never contingent on featureRailMeta being null NOW, only on it being POSSIBLE for it to go null later (a CMS edit, a future dataset reset). What was wrong originally was (a) claiming, incorrectly, that it WAS null today, and (b) the guard being a silent `if` rather than a visible `test.skip()`. Both are fixed; the guard mechanism itself stays, on its own general merits, not on the (retracted) claim about current data state.
metaLineTestDefectRuling.scopeCallOnSeedingRealDates: Moot as of the correction above. The original text considered and declined seeding real show-date data into Sanity as out-of-scope CMS work, reasoned against a null-dates premise. The dates are already populated in the live dataset (per @dev's measurement above) -- there is nothing left to seed, so this scope question does not apply to F8's current state. Kept here for the historical record of the reasoning, not as a live ruling.
